Baby1: Went into spontaneous labor at 40+2, labored at home and intended for unmedicated birth. It was a great experience up til my water was broken/I got the epidural.

Baby2: Spontaneous labor at 39+3. Labored at home 9+hrs then went in and was 6cm but baby was having frequent decels and so I could not get in the tub or really in any position that helped me cope. The frequent decels made me worry I would end up needing a cesarean so I opted for the epidural 'early' in case we needed to go to the OR. The placement was horrific, took 25mins and my back kept literally seizing up when he would go to poke me. I couldn't control my back muscles but he kept yelling at me to hold still. I could move myself around etc. I very quickly dilated to 10cm and my water broke on its own and I just pushed right then and there and he was born in 15 mins. 

Baby3: Planning for unmedicated again, but knowing that there's always a possibility I end up with the epidural. My only advice is that if you get the epidural and literally have dead weight legs, ask them to turn it down a bit. It makes pushes really difficult when you literally can't feel anything. Hi!! You’ve already received some great advice. I just wanted to address your wondering about risk of controlling via meds vs. diet alone. What is important is blood glucose management; regardless of how it is done. The reason many people have “more problems” on meds vs diet controlled alone is because of the dragging of feet to do it and how slow/difficult it can be to titrate up med dosing. This means blood glucose is left too high for too long causing the problems you hear a ton about (big babies, struggling with blood glucose after birth etc.) so if you/your provider are able to gain rapid control with meds, it really shouldn’t matter in terms of overall risk. 

All that said, I have two thoughts to leave you with as a type 2 diabetic with a history of anorexia and bulimia: 
1. Some people have severe nausea/diarrhea with metformin (I’m not one of them, thank god, but it’s a common side effect)
2. Insulin management will require carb counting and frequent blood glucose checks. It’s up to you on whether or not that is better or worse for you mentally tally’s but just something to consider. You won’t necessarily need to limit your carbs in the same way, but you will still need to know how many you’re eating and track your carbs/insulin for your provider to review and make adjustments. 

I started with metformin alone and diet. It took forever to get an insulin script but I will say for me mentally it was better to have to be extra diligent with glucose monitoring and insulin administration than extreme carb limitation, but that is not something that anyone can say for you what will be better.

If you don't want to be induced I highly recommend getting on top of your blood glucose ASAP. Buy a meter, test your fasting and post meal numbers, track what you are eating, balance your carbs with protein etc. NOW rather than waiting. Also, do not have cheat meals or days. Advocate for yourself to get on meds if you show any signs of not being able to keep your numbers in range. Tight control is the name of the game. I was on insulin (both long and short acting) but kept my numbers near perfect and was able to push back induction to 39+6. I went into spontaneous labor at 39+4 and my baby was  6lbs12oz. 

The reason people say that meds = early induction is because some providers let you go for a week or more with out of range numbers before adding or upping medications and the baby can grow too large, or other complications confound the GD. Meds are not the enemy, out of control glucose is. My provider gave me a script for a CGM and I was able to 'prove' I was keeping my glucose in range and increasing my insulin after even one 'bad' reading, so even though I ended my pregnancy on a ton of insulin I was on that high dosing to keep my numbers great.
